title: Read htaccess limits
summary: An .htaccess file can apply permitted directory settings when the server allows overrides. It is not always enabled or needed.
introduction: An .htaccess file can apply permitted directory settings when the server allows overrides. It is not always enabled or needed. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: An .htaccess file can apply permitted directory settings when the server allows overrides. It is not always enabled or needed.

blocks.code:
Server-level choice: AllowOverride None
Result: .htaccess overrides are not used for that directory
blocks.title: Read htaccess limits

blocks.text: Using central configuration can be clearer when you control the server. A hosted environment may allow selected overrides instead.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why copying an .htaccess snippet may do nothing on a given host.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not enable every override merely to make an unfamiliar snippet work.
For more detail later, use this [Apache HTTP Server further reading](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/getting-started.html).
